# TrainLens 0.19.2

This stability release makes portable-run CI checks safer, aligns metric selectors across
the CLI and Python APIs, and improves checkpoint isolation and long-run storage.

## Fixes

- CI metric gates now use split-qualified, finite metrics. Missing baseline metrics
  fail checks unless explicitly acknowledged with `--allow-removed`.
- Checkpoint selection rejects all known held-out test split aliases and preserves
  original observation indices when skipping non-finite observations.
- Project queries avoid redundant index parsing. `Project.repair()` diagnoses
  dangling entries and orphan files after interrupted operations; cleanup is opt-in.
- Run-file removal writes the index before deletion, making interruptions recoverable.
- `MonitorConfig(max_observations=N)` optionally bounds history and deduplication
  memory for long runs. The default behavior remains unchanged.
- Agent verification exposes `has_valid_evidence_references` and explicitly
  distinguishes citation checking from proving scientific or causal validity.

## Compatibility

No supported APIs have been removed. The only deliberate stricter default is
that `trainlens check --against` fails when a baseline metric disappears.
Use `--allow-removed` if this is an intentional change.

Requires Python 3.11–3.14.
